extracted.intended_audience: Interested parties, stakeholders, scientists, land managers, conservation organizations, and members of the public who may submit information or comments to the Fish and Wildlife Service docket FWS-R8-ES-2023-0052
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for submitting information and comments in response to a Federal Register reopening of the proposed rule to list the Bi-State DPS of greater sage-grouse as threatened and to designate critical habitat. Covers what topics and types of evidence the agency is specifically requesting and procedural instructions for submission and handling of comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods and docket identification
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit written comments by one of the following methods: (1) Electronically via the Federal eRulemaking Portal (https://www.regulations.gov) by entering docket FWS–R8–ES–2023–0052 and clicking 'Comment'; or (2) By hard copy to the specified U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service mailing address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We request that you send comments only by the methods described above. The docket number for this reopened comment period is FWS–R8–ES–2023–0052.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of existing submissions / do not resubmit previous comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments previously submitted need not be resubmitted, as they will be fully considered in preparing the final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please do not resubmit comments or information already provided on the proposed rules during the initial or subsequent comment periods; such comments are incorporated as part of the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness (comment close date)
rubrics_metrics.description: So that we can fully consider your comments in our final determination, submit your comments on or before June 26, 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting information (substantive comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions merely stating support for, or opposition to, the action under consideration without providing supporting information do not provide substantial information necessary to support a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 4(b)(1)(A) of the Act directs that determinations must be made solely on the basis of the best scientific and commercial data available; therefore comments should include data, references, analyses, or specific information rather than only assertions of support/opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best scientific and commercial data standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Any listing determination we make must be made based on the best available information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To inform the status review, the Service requests new information that has become available since the publication of the 2013 proposed rules; submit objective scientific or commercial data, analyses, and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting and personal information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: We will post all comments on https://www.regulations.gov. This generally means that we will post any personal information you provide us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submit information via Regulations.gov, your entire comment—including any personal identifying information—will be posted. If submission is made via hardcopy containing personal identifying information, you may request at the top of your document that we withhold this information from public review, but we cannot guarantee we will be able to do so. Agencies review submissions and may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biology, range, and population trends (requested data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information concerning the Bi-State DPS's biology, range, and population trends, including biological or ecological requirements, genetics and taxonomy, historical and current range (including locations of additional leks), population levels and trends, and past and ongoing conservation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Service is particularly interested in: (a) habitat requirements for feeding, breeding, and sheltering; (b) genetics and taxonomy; (c) distribution patterns and locations of any additional leks; (d) historical and current population levels and projected trends; and (e) past and ongoing conservation measures for the Bi-State DPS, its habitat, or both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threats and conservation actions (requested data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on threats and conservation actions affecting the species, including factors that may affect the species' continued existence and biological, commercial trade, or other data concerning threats (or lack thereof), and existing regulations or conservation actions addressing threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of factors include habitat modification or destruction, overutilization, disease, predation, inadequacy of existing regulatory mechanisms, or other natural or manmade factors. Provide relevant data on threats or mitigation actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and current status (additional information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information concerning the historical and current status of the Bi-State DPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide records, analyses, or other documentation that clarify historical distribution, past population baselines, or recent status changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory recommendations for section 4(d) rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on regulations that may be necessary and advisable to provide for the conservation of the Bi-State DPS and that the Service can consider in developing a section 4(d) rule for the species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, submit information concerning the extent to which the Service should include any of the section 9 prohibitions in the 4(d) rule or whether to consider any additional exceptions from the prohibitions in the 4(d) rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidental take provision in 4(d) rule (agriculture/conservation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Service should add a provision to the proposed 4(d) rule that covers incidental take of the Bi-State DPS in accordance with agricultural or conservation activities consistent with the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples, evidence, or analyses supporting inclusion/exclusion of incidental-take provisions tied to agricultural or conservation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of ongoing conservation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on the effectiveness of ongoing conservation measures and management actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide monitoring results, evaluation studies, or other evidence that demonstrates the conservation measures' outcomes or gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current habitat conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on current habitat conditions including but not limited to quality of upland and meadow or riparian sites, presence and abundance of annual invasive grasses and weeds or other increasing plants (e.g., conifer trees), and recovery of previously burned sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information may include larger landscape-scale assessments or smaller site-specific investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount and distribution of habitat; criteria for critical habitat inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific information on the amount and distribution of habitat for the Bi-State DPS and any additional areas occurring within the species' range that should be included in the critical habitat designation because they (i) are occupied at the time of listing and contain the physical or biological features essential to conservation and may require special management, or (ii) are unoccupied at the time of listing and are essential for conservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide spatial data, maps, habitat-feature descriptions, and analyses evaluating whether unoccupied areas would, with reasonable certainty, contribute to conservation and contain at least one essential physical or biological feature. Include special management considerations (e.g., for climate change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special management considerations for proposed critical habitat
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about special management considerations or protection that may be needed in critical habitat areas being proposed, including managing for the potential effects of climate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe management actions, projected climate impacts, or restoration needs specific to proposed critical habitat units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land use designations and planned activities impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on land use designations and current or planned activities in the subject areas and their possible impacts on proposed critical habitat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide land-use plans, project proposals, timing, intensity, and documented or modeled impacts to habitat or species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probable economic, national security, or other impacts of designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any probable economic, national security, or other relevant impacts of designating any area that may be included in the final designation, and the related benefits of including or excluding specific areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide economic data, national-security considerations, and analyses of benefits and costs tied to inclusion or exclusion of specific areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on draft economic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on the extent to which the description of probable economic impacts in the draft economic analysis (available in docket FWS–R8–ES–2013–0042) is a reasonable estimate and any additional information regarding probable economic impacts that should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast draft analysis assumptions with updated data, supply alternative estimates, or provide information on costs not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information supporting exclusions under section 4(b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether any specific areas proposed for critical habitat designation should be considered for exclusion under section 4(b)(2) of the Act, and whether the benefits of potentially excluding any specific area outweigh the benefits of including that area under section 4(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recommending exclusions, provide information supporting a benefit of exclusion (e.g., conservation partnerships, economic impacts, national security).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving public participation and understanding in critical habitat designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Service could improve or modify its approach to designating critical habitat in any way to provide for greater public participation and understanding, or to better accommodate public concerns and comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer concrete suggestions for outreach, analysis presentation, mapping tools, comment processes, or alternative procedures that would increase transparency and stakeholder engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of review and potential outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the Service will consider all comments and information received, final determinations may differ from the current proposal; the Service may determine the species is endangered instead of threatened, not warranted for listing, may change critical habitat boundaries, or may change prohibitions/exceptions in the 4(d) rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information that could affect status determination (e.g., new threats, new conservation evidence, quantitative analyses) to be considered in the Species Status Assessment and final rule.
